As I've already said, I like to game, and I do like to use max settings when possible. Not all of my games are compatible with Linux, and WINE doesn't have the best performance, especially for newer games. So, making a full switch to Linux and ditching Windows isn't really an option. I could dual boot Windows and Linux, but I'm not in the mood of rebooting my PC every time I decide to play some games or do my homework or w/e. Sure, the loading would be fast since I'm using an SSD, it's just the rebooting that bothers me.

Then out of nowhere I stumbled upon a third option: coLinux. I'm not yet entirely sure how it works, but I think it's like running a Linux distro as a program, inside Windows. So no virtualization like Virtualbox. If this allows me to run both Windows and Linux at the same time, and both have good access to my hardware, then this might be the golden solution I'm looking for. If it is, then I'm willing to put some effort into getting Linux Mint running like this.

I'd like to hear your opinions on coLinux, or alternative solutions. What's the performance like? What about privacy, i.e. can Microsoft "see" what I'm doing in coLinux, could they intercept my internet traffic? What are the limitations, possible complications? Anything relevant.

Thanks in advance.

Section 3: Flairs

Flairs can be applied liberally since they can be changed at will. The only one that might require conservative use is Opinion / Analysis since most news articles would be incredibly short/boring to read with some sort of speculation or analysis. Most current news outlets tend to use both.

  • Aggregator - A news source that aggregates articles from other news sources. Examples of this are the New York Times and Yahoo News

  • Meta - Self-Describing. Never used this one, but will probably get use in the future since @system owns the subverse and users may want to show input. Should come with a guideline for using this in the future.

  • Opinion / Analysis - Primarily used when "inside sources" are cited about an event that they say will happen in the future. A great example of this is stocks, currency, and other forms of tradegood speculation. Additional examples of this are OP-ed articles, or articles examining an event in depth bringing little to no news to the surface.

  • Paywalled Content - Articles or sites that are either completely blocked by a paywall, or have a limited number of articles available to view for free for the day. Prime examples of this are the Wall Street Journal(wsj.com) and The Telegraph (telegraph.co.uk). After marking it with this flair, it is good community service to archive the topic (using archive.is or similar service) for users who are blocked by the paywall, or do not want to support the paywall.

This flair is actually meant for titles that are mostly inaccurate as to their content, as opposed to sensationalist. Gnome Druid (Circle of Moon) is probably the strongest early game build possible once you hit level 3 (taking 1 level into barbarian). Shape shift into Bear at level 2, hits twice, has 34 (-ish?) health on top of the gnome's default health, half damage from barbarian and extra damage on attacks, advantage on all saving throws that aren't Dexterity or Constitution.

At level 3:

About 56 health (34 while in bear form)A Barbarian should have about 35, for comparison.

11 AC (or about 12 in humanoid form)

Takes half damage on all physical attacks

Advantage for all strength checks and all saving throws that aren't Dex or Con (Barbarian and Gnome bonuses).

Attacks twice, 1d8+4+2(rage) and 2d6+4+2(rage), that's 23 damage per round, +6 to hit.

I always mentally groan when I hear players rolling a gnomish druid/barbarian (Barb is better to start), since it means they're going for a min-max playstyle. Now, the idea of a gnome becoming larger and scarier than you is pretty cool and probably was thought of more than once, but be aware of the potential headache it can bring if you are less prepared than your players are.
